Which of the following was not a part of the challenges that were faced by
independent India?

options.text:
The first and the immediate challenge was to shape a nation that was
united.
The second challenge was to establish democracy.

The third challenge was to ensure the development and well-being of the
entire society and not only of some sections.

The fourth challenge was to provide freedom and sovereignty to Princely
States.

solution.quick: Independent India faced three primary nation-building challenges (unity, democracy, and inclusive development); providing sovereignty to Princely States was never a national goal.
solution.concept: The foundational 'Three Challenges' of nation-building in independent India.

questionText:
Which of the following is not a difference between forest movements of the
South and those of the North?

options.text:
The forests in the South are still peopled while the forest in the North is
more or less devoid of human habitat

The North believes in the notion of wilderness as a wild place. No such
idea is prevailing in the South

Wilderness campaigns were initiated in the South. In contrast, in the
North there are has no such camapigns

For the North, 'environment is perceived as something that should be
protected from humans.
However, environmental issues in the South are based on the assumption
that people live in the forests.

solution.quick: Wilderness preservation campaigns were initiated and championed in the industrialised North (e.g. USA, Europe), not in the Global South.

Analysis: NCERT Class 12 Contemporary World Politics (Chapter 8: Environment and Natural Resources, 'Environmental Movements: One or Many?', p. 121): 'Forest movements in the South are very different from those in the North. Therefore, claiming that wilderness campaigns originated in the South is factually incorrect.'
